newsitem.title: UK: Lira up on EMU talk, London shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Lira up on EMU talk, London shares higher.

text.p: The Italian lira firmed on the mark on Friday after a senior banking source in Frankfurt said that Rome had requested a European Union monetary meeting on Saturday to discuss the currency's re-entry into the EU exchange rate mechanism.
On the European bourses, London shares rose strongly amid selective buying, while French and German shares took their cue from Wall Street's overnight dip and fell before turning mixed.
The lira, which has strengthened in recent days, was quoted at around 996 to the mark at midday on Friday compared with 999 on Thursday.

Italian government sources and a European Commission spokesman declined to confirm or deny there would be a weekend meeting of the key European Union monetary committee, which normally convenes in Brussels.
But a senior banking source told Reuters in Frankfurt: "The Italians have requested a meeting of the monetary committee for tomorrow."
In other currency developments, the dollar blipped above the 1.50 level against the mark, but weakened against the yen on reports that Japan's discount rate is too low and may rise soon.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, was more than one percent higher at midday as strong gains in energy and utility stocks outweighed worries about interest rates and next week's budget, dealers said.
"This market is just unbelievable...we think people are trying to level books ahead of the budget and think one or two were caught short," one trader said.

The FTSE 100 index, confounding early expectations of a drift downwards after a generally lacklustre week, was up 40.8 points at 3,994.6 just before midday, with gainers heavily outnumbering losers on a wave of short covering.
But dealers cautioned that volume, at just over 218 million shares, remained modest and said a strong gain on the December FTSE futures contract was dragging the market higher.

Utility and energy stocks led the market, with nuclear electricity generator British Energy hitting new highs on a favourable write-up in the Financial Times Lex column on the company's cash generating strength.

The stock, among London's 10 most-active shares with over five million shares trading, was up 16-1/2p at 151p in late morning trade. Other generators gained, notably PowerGen, up four pence at 591p and National Power, up 14p at 465p.

But dealers said there was still scepticism about the market and warned that attention was likely to drift back to the threat of the pound's strength and the danger that finance minister Kenneth Clarke might be tempted into pre-election tax cuts.
In Frankfurt, German shares were still down some 0.4 percent around lunchtime after starting bourse dealings lower on the back of Wall Street's weaker close on Thursday.
After setting November's 10th record high on Wednesday, Wall Street's Dow Jones index slipped 11.55 points to 6,418.47 as modest profit-taking dragged it back from record highs.
German dealers said business was thin and the market was consolidating after recent gains. Deutsche Telekom weakened further after falling in New York overnight.
French shares regained some of their early modest losses, and drifted back into positive ground by early afternoon.
Traders said franc weakness along with a cautious Wall Street were factors weighing on the market.
CURRENCIES AT 1300 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.30 yen and 1.5017 marks against 111.43 yen and 1.4980 marks late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1300 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 40.8 points at 3,994.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 4.47 points at 2,238.04.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 8.65 points at 2,763.69.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened firmer at $376.90 against $376.65 at the London close on Thursday. Good physical demand in Europe helped prices. ($1=.5940 Pound)
